# Physiology, Platelet Activation

**Authors:** Jennifer Saad, Edinen Asuka, Lisa Schoenberger

**Source:** StatPearls - StatPearls Publishing

## Abstract

Blood vessels must maintain their integrity to effectively deliver blood to the body’s vital organs and tissues. When damage occurs to the walls of a blood vessel, the physiological, reparative mechanism of hemostasis prevents further bleeding. Hemostasis occurs in 2 phases: platelet activation to form a static plug and stabilization of this plug through extrinsic and intrinsic coagulation pathways, known as primary and secondary hemostasis, respectively. This topic reviews the physiological components of platelet activation during primary hemostasis.
